samples.summary: No test covers the `googleStrategyProvider` factory that decides whether the Google passport strategy is registered at all
samples.evidence: `auth.module.ts:55-60` adds a `useFactory` provider whose whole purpose (per its own 30-line comment) is to fix a regression where the module-scope evaluation ran before dotenv and left `AuthGuard('google')` failing with "Unknown authentication strategy". There is no `auth.module.spec.ts` (glob of `packages/backend/src/auth/*.ts` shows specs for controller, service, guards, strategies, cli-auth store, oauth-state, login-return-path — none for the module), and no backend e2e boots `AuthModule` against Google env (grep for `AuthModule` in `packages/backend/test/*` and `src/**/*.spec.ts` finds only `auth.module.ts` and `app.module.ts`). So nothing asserts (a) that a configured deployment actually constructs `GoogleStrategy` (registering 'google' with passport) or (b) that an unconfigured one returns `null` without throwing `OAuth2Strategy requires a clientID option` at boot. Both failure modes are user-visible: Google login 500s, or the whole app fails to start.

samples.summary: `googleAuthPartiallyConfigured()` / `missingGoogleAuthVars()` and the boot warning they feed have no test
samples.evidence: `oauth-providers.ts` has no spec file (no `oauth-providers.spec.ts` in the auth dir listing), and the only exercise of the module is indirect through `controller.authProviders()` and `GoogleAuthGuard` (both of which only touch `googleAuthConfigured()`). The half-configured branch — the one thing the `AuthModule` constructor warning exists for (`auth.module.ts:98-104`) — is never exercised, so a wrong boundary (e.g. `set > 0` vs `>= 0`, or a wrong variable name in the list) ships silently. Failure is contained to a missing/incorrect log line.

samples.summary: `GoogleCallbackGuard` is only tested for the 404 path; nothing asserts it does not mint a fresh state cookie
samples.evidence: The single `GoogleCallbackGuard` test (`google-auth.guard.spec.ts:73-79`) calls it with `configure({})` so it throws before any other logic. The guard's distinguishing property versus `GoogleAuthGuard` is that it must NOT call `startWebOAuthLogin` — minting a new `oauthStateCookieName()` cookie on the callback would overwrite the secret the controller is about to compare, silently converting the CSRF check into a self-fulfilling one. No test with Google configured asserts `res.cookie` was not called for the callback guard.

samples.summary: The extracted `finishWebLogin` returnTo branch (clear cookie + redirect to the stored path) is untested at either callback
samples.evidence: `finishWebLogin` reads `req.cookies[loginReturnCookieName()]`, clears it and feeds it to `loginRedirectUrl(..., safeReturnPath(...))`. The new Google test's `googleRequest()` (auth.controller.spec.ts:~492) only ever supplies state cookies, and asserts `res.redirect('http://localhost:5173')`; grep for `login_return` / `loginRedirectUrl` in `packages/backend/src` finds hits only in `login-return-path.spec.ts` (unit tests of the helpers) and the controller itself. So the controller-level wiring — that a stored returnTo actually changes the post-login redirect and that the cookie is cleared — has no coverage on the path this diff refactored.

samples.summary: `fetchAuthProviders`' non-OK branch and its defensive body coercion are untested
samples.evidence: The page tests in `login-form.test.tsx:115-186` stub fetch with `{ ok: true, json }` or a rejection, covering only the success and throw paths. Nothing exercises `if (!res.ok) return fallback` or the coercions `github: body.github !== false` / `google: body.google === true` (e.g. a body of `{ google: "true" }` must stay false). A regression there would either hide the Google button on configured installs or show a 404-leading button.

samples.summary: The Google photo fallback `profile._json?.picture` has no test
samples.evidence: `google.strategy.spec.ts` always supplies `photos: [{ value: ... }]` (makeProfile line 26) and the only photo assertion is in the happy-path `toEqual` at line 51. The `?? profile._json?.picture` branch — the one Google profiles without a `photos` array hit — is never exercised, so an avatar silently going missing would not be caught.

samples.summary: The GitHub `validate` return shape is only asserted on `.email`; the other fields it still has to carry are unchecked
samples.evidence: The new `GitHubStrategy verified email` block (`github.strategy.spec.ts:129-176`) asserts only `user.email` (or that it throws). Unlike the Google spec, which uses a full `toEqual`, nothing pins `githubId`, `username`, `photo` or `accessToken` after this diff restructured the destructuring in `validate`, so dropping one of them would pass the suite while breaking user creation.

samples.summary: Google happy-path only asserts two fields of the `findOrCreateUser` payload
samples.evidence: `expect(userService.findOrCreateUser).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ authProvider: 'google', email: 'ada@example.com' }))` leaves `username` and `photo` unchecked, though the controller explicitly maps them (auth.controller.ts:280-285) and `username` is what `findOrCreateUser` slugs the new workspace name from.

finding.summary: No test covers the `googleStrategyProvider` factory that decides whether the Google passport strategy is registered at all
finding.evidence: `auth.module.ts:55-60` adds a `useFactory` provider whose whole purpose (per its own 30-line comment) is to fix a regression where the module-scope evaluation ran before dotenv and left `AuthGuard('google')` failing with "Unknown authentication strategy". There is no `auth.module.spec.ts` (glob of `packages/backend/src/auth/*.ts` shows specs for controller, service, guards, strategies, cli-auth store, oauth-state, login-return-path — none for the module), and no backend e2e boots `AuthModule` against Google env (grep for `AuthModule` in `packages/backend/test/*` and `src/**/*.spec.ts` finds only `auth.module.ts` and `app.module.ts`). So nothing asserts (a) that a configured deployment actually constructs `GoogleStrategy` (registering 'google' with passport) or (b) that an unconfigured one returns `null` without throwing `OAuth2Strategy requires a clientID option` at boot. Both failure modes are user-visible: Google login 500s, or the whole app fails to start.

verdict.reason: The `googleStrategyProvider` useFactory exists at packages/backend/src/auth/auth.module.ts:55-60 and is the sole thing that decides whether `GoogleStrategy`'s constructor runs (and therefore whether passport learns the 'google' strategy). No test anywhere in the repo exercises it. Repo-wide greps for `AuthModule`, `googleStrategyProvider`, `GoogleStrategy`, and `googleAuthConfigured|oauth-providers` return zero test files touching the module or its config predicate; there is no auth.module.spec.ts among the 29 files in src/auth. google.strategy.spec.ts:13-17 bypasses the factory entirely by constructing the strategy by hand, so it passes regardless of which branch the factory takes. auth.controller.spec.ts:611-633 and google-auth.guard.spec.ts:23-64 cover the per-request answers (`GET /auth/providers`, guard 404), not the injector-time registration that the 30-line comment says had drifted out of sync with them. The 13 DB-backed e2e suites that import AppModule (e.g. authenticated-http.e2e-spec.ts:62) instantiate the factory transitively, but never set GOOGLE_* env and assert nothing about Google (grep for auth/google|auth/providers|GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID across packages/backend/test returns nothing), so they cover neither the configured branch nor the claim that 'google' is registered. Major: an undetected failure of either branch means Google login 500s with "Unknown authentication strategy" or every non-Google deployment fails to boot with "OAuth2Strategy requires a clientID option".

finding.summary: LoginPage's new provider-fetch wiring is never exercised: the stub returns `google: false`, which equals the component's initial state
finding.evidence: `page.tsx` adds `useEffect(() => fetchAuthProviders().then(p => setGoogleEnabled(p.google)))` and passes `googleEnabled` into `LoginForm`. The only LoginPage tests stub fetch with `{ github: true, google: false }` (login-form.test.tsx:117-125) and assert nothing about providers. Since `useState(false)` is the initial value, deleting the whole effect, mis-reading `providers.google`, or never passing the prop would leave both LoginPage tests green. The `googleEnabled=true` rendering is only tested by passing the prop directly to `LoginForm` (line 62), which bypasses the new page logic entirely. Net effect: a broken wiring ships as "Google button never appears" on every deployment that configured Google, with no failing test.

verdict.reason: The finding claims LoginPage's provider-fetch wiring has no test that could fail, because the only stub returns `google: false` (equal to the initial state). That is factually wrong about the file it cites. login-form.test.tsx:146-157 contains "offers Google once the backend says the deployment has it", which calls `stubProviders({ github: true, google: true })` — overriding the `beforeEach` default at line 132 — renders the real `LoginPage` via `renderPage` (lines 123-129), and then asserts (a) a "continue with google" link actually appears with an href containing `/auth/google`, and (b) fetch was called with a URL containing `/auth/providers`. This test fails under every mutation the finding enumerates: deleting the useEffect (page.tsx:27-35), mis-reading `providers.google` (page.tsx:30), or not passing `googleEnabled` to LoginForm (page.tsx:72) all leave `googleEnabled` false so `findByRole` times out. Complementary branches are covered too: line 159 asserts Google stays off for `google: false`, and line 174 asserts the fetch-rejection path degrades to GitHub-only, matching the fallback in api/auth.ts:150-167. The reviewer apparently read only the `beforeEach` stub at line 132 and missed the per-test override. Not a vacuous or missing test.
